newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo could export one mln T maize, official says.
newsitem.headline: Yugo could export one mln T maize, official says.

text.p: Yugoslavia could export one million tonnes of maize from this year's harvest which is expected to beat last year's despite prolonged drought, a senior government official said on Friday.

"Yugoslavia could export one million tonnes of maize if the latest experts' estimates of 5.5 million to six million tonnes of maize crop come true," said Milan Prostran, undersecretary in the federal Agriculture Ministry.
This year the maize area increased to about 1.5 million hectares from 1.38 million in 1995. Last year's maize crop was 5.7 million tonnes.
"But maize is a strange crop," Prostran said. "You should not trust it (regarding yield) before you actually harvest it."
A senior official in the Maize Institute in Belgrade agreed that the maize harvest could total six million tonnes this year despite long dry summer periods,
"We expect the maize harvest to be at least at last year's level and even a few hundred thousand tonnes above," Zivorad Videnovic, deputy general director of the Maize Institute, told Reuters.

"We were very cautious in our earlier forecasts due to drought which reduced the production in eastern parts of the republic by 25 percent," he said. "But yield in the western parts of the country is expected to be a record high, so that is why we forecast about six million tonnes."
The institute's forecast is the same as that of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce, which said it expects a six million tonne crop of maize with an average yield of 4.2 tonnes per hectare.
"This is an increase of 300,000 tonnes against last year's production," said Tihomir Madic at the Chamber.
"Weather and insufficient irrigation systems are the main factors which determine maize yield here," he said.
State co-operatives are expected to produce 700,000 tonnes and farmers about 5.3 million tonnes this year.
These forecasts are well above the statistic's office estimates of 4.95 million tonnes of maize and the average yield of 3.44 tonnes per hectare.
Prostran said the area under maize remained more or less the same over the years, but the yield per hectare fell.
"Yugoslavia (now comprising Serbia and Montenegro) used to produce 7-8 million tonnes of maize a year with an average yield of 5 tonnes per hectare." he said.
Maize acreage in the past ranged from 1.35 - 1.55 million hectares with average yield of 3.0 to 5.7 tonnes per hectare. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
